title: Catalog branches: Proof strip
topics: Linked lists, binary trees and search trees
summary: The input is a binary search tree with distinct values. Produce its values in the inclusive range [k,k+12], in ascending order, pruning subtrees that cannot meet that range. Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.
descriptionMd:
An ordered folder tree can skip entire branches outside the inspector's requested number range. Pia rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

The input is a binary search tree with distinct values. Produce its values in the inclusive range [k,k+12], in ascending order, pruning subtrees that cannot meet that range.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement catalogBranchesProofStrip(root, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: BST range pruning. The input is a binary search tree with distinct values. Produce its values in the inclusive range [k,k+12], in ascending order, pruning subtrees that cannot meet that range. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 0 <= node count <= 31; JSON null placeholders do not count as nodes.
1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
Lists are acyclic. Trees use level-order JSON with null for missing children; [] is an empty root. The runner supplies nodes with val/next or val/left/right.

Target time O(h + r); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
